newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba rights claw back losses, end higher.
newsitem.headline: Ciba rights claw back losses, end higher.

text.p: Subscription rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals Holding Inc clawed back early losses to end higher in busy trading on nearly frantic last-minute demand from foreign investors, dealers said.

Rights for Ciba SC, being spun off via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders, closed at 103.50 Swiss francs ($70.21), up two francs and well above the 90 francs per right bid price set on Monday night by a bank consortium.
"There are some desperate investors who want to be assured of some stock. We expected this. Some people from the U.S. mainly, I think," one banker familiar with the transaction said.
Volume was high at 461 million Swiss francs worth of rights.
Analysts called the 90 franc bid fundamentally appropriate.

Rights opened down to 92.50 as a wave of "best" sell orders flooded the market, one dealer said. Trading was twice halted for the mandatory 15 minutes because of sharp price movements. But rights rallied in late trading.

"Today I would have expected more selling pressure, but in general we had a strong demand book and the reaction from investors in pre-marketing and then in the road show was extremely good," the banker said.

"From the outset we had a general feeling of scarcity in the market, of people who wanted to assure stock. It was not such a surprise that these levels were reached. The name Ciba is certainly very strong and has helped very much."

Nevertheless, the implied PEs at this level for the rights puts Ciba SC at a premium to Clariant and other specialty chemical companies in Europe. The rights price values Ciba SC shares at 113.50 francs and the company at some 8.2 billion francs.
"It is certainly a very high level at which it will be difficult to have a strong after-market performance," the banker said. "I don't see much room upwards in the short term."

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion francs from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's market leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.

The consortium will use the rights it acquires to buy shares in Ciba SC that will then be resold in a global offering with at least 300 million francs worth of stock. Pricing and allocation are set to be announced on March 13 at 0700 GMT.
"Whatever we have to place from the global offer of shares will be placed like a secondary offering, at a small discount to the last trading price, if any discount," the banker said.
Global coordinators UBS and CSFB said last week shares may be priced above the range of 72 to 86 francs first indicated for the global offering given higher prices for the rights.
-- Michael Shields, Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340 ($ = 1.474 Swiss Francs)
